LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 9.3.1 WORD SETS (GENDER SETS FOR ANIMALS/PEOPLE) OPPOSITES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn words referring to male and female animals/people?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Writing skills as they write sentences correctly using gender sets.

● Communication and Collaboration: Teamwork as learners actively engage in discussions with peers about words referring to gender sets of

animals or people.

Values:
Respect : Acceptance as the learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers during discussions

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication as learner identifies gender sets of animals and people.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the knowledge of gender sets to what is learnt in Kenya Sign Language Activities.
